text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 and the common cold are both respiratory illnesses, but they are caused by different viruses. While some symptoms overlap, there are key differences in their onset and severity. COVID-19 symptoms typically appear 2-14 days after exposure, whereas common cold symptoms appear 1-3 days after exposure. COVID-19 can also cause more severe illness and complications compared to the common cold.
